text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- President Ulmanis, on a visit to the U.S., received on Saturday in San Francisco an award from the Legal Initiative for Central and Eastern Europe for his contribution in strengthening democracy and developing the judicial system in Latvia.
- EU Commissioner for Agriculture and Rural Environment Franz Fischler ended a visit to Latvia, saying the country should keep the international community better informed about its achievements.
- On August 2, Latvia and Lithuania opened their first joint border crossing point.
- Volkswagen's new official dealer, Volksvagens Centrs Riga, is to start operations.

- The newspaper said that in 1994 outgoing Prime Minister Andris Shkele took a loan of 320,000 lats from Zemes banka which allowed him to privatise Baltmaiznieks, one of Latvia's major food companies.

- Two Latvian companies, Riga soft drinks and mineral water factory and rubber factory Quadrat, were on the lists of dormant account holders published by Swiss banks recently. Their successors may try and get the money back.
- Shareholders of meat plant Rigas miesnieks approved on Friday the take-over of 67 percent of the company's shares by Estonia's Rakvere.
- Subsidiaries of Latvian Shipping Company in low-tax countries showed a profit last year, while their parent company suffered a loss of $35 million.
- Price cuts by Intel have led several computer dealers in Latvia to cut their prices by 10 to 30 percent.
